column1: # SIAM 100-Digit Challenge, Appendix D Problem 20: h(h(z)) = exp(z), h(0) for the Kneser half-iterate (research problem as posed).

column4: consensus, 7 digits only: Robbins' truncated Abel system (intuitive slog) h_n(0) for n = 80,100,120,140,160 = 0.4985633095, 0.4985632904, 0.4985632855, 0.4985632851, 0.4985632851 (exact rational solve; siam100_refs/d20_ref.py + d20_ref.wl), settling at 0.49856328509(+-1e-11); the commonly quoted Kneser value h(0) = log(e^^(1/2)) = log(1.64635423375...) = 0.4985632879 (not independently verified here; Finch, arXiv:2509.24918, gives e^^(1/2) = 1.6463... for Kneser) differs at the 9th digit, so whether Robbins' limit IS Kneser's h(0) is not settled here. An attempted Kouznetsov Cauchy-integral solver (double precision) did not converge and is not used. Stored: 0.4985633 (the digits all sources share); need 5 = known - 2.
